items.text: Subscribers is the one fragile check, reading 22: the newest reading is 0.8 per 1,000 views versus a typical 1.8, carried from an older episode. Across the show DesignerTom gets 3.1 per 1,000 views, Dive Club 1.9.
items.recommendation: Add one spoken subscribe ask at the busiest chat moment and one at sign-off, naming the channel each viewer is on. Pin the subscribe link in both chats. Vary the wording weekly and compare subscribers per 1,000 views on each channel.

items.text: E13 (still in its first weeks): 3.4 of every 100 viewers left about seven minutes in, during setup talk about a question widget, and 4.1 more around a tenth in. A website walkthrough about a fifth in held 2.3 extra.
items.recommendation: Open the next episode with the guest topic or a screen demo in the first five minutes, and move housekeeping asks past the first third. Then compare early exits against this episode to see whether the change helped.

items.text: Search and suggested videos bring a share of 7.6 on the latest reading (from an older finished episode) versus a typical 14.3, and YouTube search is only 4.9 of whole-show views. Discovery is softening.
items.recommendation: Rewrite the next two episode titles and descriptions around the plain phrase a designer would search, such as the guest's topic or tool, and add chapter markers. Test it against your current titling and watch the search share.

items.text: Live turnout is healthy: average 113 live viewers versus a typical 74, peak 142 versus 97.5, and 79.6 chatters per 100 viewers versus 53.9.
items.recommendation: Keep the format and announce timing behind this live week, and write down what changed (guest, clip, announce time) so you can repeat it. Hold off on new segments until subscribers recover, so any change stays easy to read.

items.text: Goodwill reads healthy at 91, but LinkedIn viewers of a live call-in segment wrote that they couldn't hear the caller.
items.recommendation: Run a caller audio test before going live and have a host repeat each caller's key line. In the first minute of the next call-in, ask viewers to confirm in chat that they can hear.
